networkInputOwnership.scope: Future application RAF callbacks were held after a canonical frame barrier, with timers and live network/authority left running and the pending input window drained first. This demonstrates RAF coupling of command admission, not an OS/GPU stall, FPS cost or an exact lost-command count. The QA gate subsequently gained submission/ACK/tick progression requirements for future independent-mode runs; those additional fields were not captured in this historical report.

renderClock.status: adopted; Game focused402, typecheck/build, native score and separate movement/RAF gate complete
renderClock.cause: A queued RAF timestamp can predate a performance.now() reset on resume, visibility, studio exit or benchmark entry. The former Math.min(.1,(now-last)/1000) could become negative, reduce fixed-step debt and grow the visual correction exp(-dt*15). Source and deterministic regression prove the branch; this run did not measure a negative dt in a native production frame.
renderClock.change: A persistent clock returns zero for stale/equal timestamps and retains its reset baseline. Ordinary positive timestamps retain the exact original subtraction, division and 0.1 second cap. No extra per-frame clock read, timer or allocation is added.
limits: This fixes stale/reset frame time only; production input is still owned by RAF.
Server60Hz, vehicle120Hz, motor1/60, six-step cap, input48 window, visual settings and entity population are unchanged.
No FPS improvement or absence of long frames is established by these unit tests.
